policies.title: Costa Rica: 2025 first and second group ordinary passports visa-free
policies.summary: Resolution AJ-484-11-2025 expressly places these nationalities in the first or second visa-free group. Only catalog country codes are mapped; territory/dependency wording conditioned on another country’s passport is not expanded.
conditions: First-group admission is up to 180 days non-extendable, subject to the stated limited extension rule; second-group admission is up to 30 days, extendable up to 90.

First-group passports require the directive’s stated validity; second-group passports require at least 90 days. Honduras has a police-certificate condition; Salvador and Russia have their expressly stated special rules.

Machine-readable/biometric document, funds, return/onward ticket and admission controls apply. No residence, work, transit, crew, diplomatic, official/service, special-document or individual treatment is established.

policies.title: Costa Rica: consular, restricted and residual foreign ordinary passports require advance visa
policies.summary: Resolution AJ-484-11-2025 expressly puts named nationalities into consular or restricted groups and puts every country not named in a group into the restricted group. The normalized baseline is advance visa required; this is not eVisa or visa on arrival.
conditions: Third-group consular visas and fourth-group Commission-authorized restricted visas are single-entry, passport-stamped advance visas; both normally allow up to 30 days subject to the directive.

The directive’s special China, Colombia, Nicaragua and Venezuela provisions and all US/Canada/Japan/Schengen/EEA/UK multiple-entry visa or residence-document exceptions are conditional and are not normalized as passport-wide access.

Passport validity, funds, onward ticket, no-entry-ban and border admissibility requirements apply. Residence, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official/service and special-document routes are excluded.

unresolved.reason: Resolution AJ-484-11-2025 governs persons extranjeras/non-residents and does not directly establish the Costa Rican citizenship/right-of-entry status for the catalog’s CR→CR pair.
